question_text: If −1, 2, α are the roots of 2x³ + x² − 7x − 6 = 0, then find α.

recall_prompt: Say which root relation you would use to find α, and what it gives.
insider_note: The leading coefficient is 2, so the sum is −1/2, not −1; that division is the whole question.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Sum of roots
steps.margin_note: First mark. Two roots known; the sum relation S₁ = −a₁/a₀ = −1/2 gives the third. Note a₀ = 2, not 1.

recall.must_convey: That the sum of the three roots is −a₁/a₀ = −1/2.
accept: the sum of the roots is minus a one by a naught which is minus half
use the sum of roots, minus the x squared coefficient over the leading coefficient
S one equals minus one by two
roots sum minus a one by a naught, ante minus half
sum of the three roots is minus one by two
heard_as: minus a one by a naught

steps.why: With two roots known, one relation with the third root in it is enough. The sum is the simplest; the product (−1)(2)α = −a₃/a₀ = 3 is the check.
common_mistakes: Dividing by 1 instead of by the leading coefficient 2.

steps.label: Find α
steps.margin_note: Second mark. −1 + 2 + α = −1/2 gives α = −3/2. Check with the product: (−1)(2)(−3/2) = 3 = −a₃/a₀ = 6/2.

accept: minus one plus two plus alpha is minus half so alpha is minus three by two
alpha equals minus three by two
one plus alpha equals minus half, alpha is minus one and a half
minus one plus two plus alpha minus half, kabatti alpha minus three by two
the third root is minus three halves

steps.why: The product relation is the free check: (−1)(2)(−3/2) = 3 = −a₃/a₀. Two relations agreeing is how a three-line answer proves itself.
common_mistakes: Writing α = −1/2 − 1 = −3/2 with a sign slip as +3/2.
